events.title: US military operation topples Maduro, sets hemispheric tone
events.detail: US forces launched a military assault on Venezuela, capturing President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores and extraditing them to New York. The operation, framed by Washington as a counter-narco-terrorism action, left more than 100 dead including civilians, and is widely read as the opening move of the 'Trump Corollary' to the Monroe Doctrine that the Shield of the Americas would later formalize.
events.confidenceReason: US government confirms the operation and Maduro's capture; casualty figures (100+) come from secondary reporting and are contested by human rights monitors.

events.title: Colombia reinforces Venezuela border after US strike
events.detail: Colombia deployed additional troops to its border with Venezuela in the immediate aftermath of the US operation against Maduro, citing instability and possible cross-border spillover from Venezuelan security forces and armed groups.

events.title: Three boat strikes kill 11 in Pacific and Caribbean
events.detail: US Southern Command carried out three lethal strikes on small vessels in the eastern Pacific and Caribbean in a single day, killing 11 people SOUTHCOM said were engaged in narcotics smuggling. The strikes were part of Operation Southern Spear, the kinetic campaign that would become the operational backbone of the coalition founded weeks later; the campaign has killed at least 190 people in more than 50 strikes since September 2025.
events.confidenceReason: SOUTHCOM confirms strikes and target identification as traffickers; independent verification of each vessel's cargo/intent is not possible.

events.title: Joint Security Declaration signed at SOUTHCOM headquarters
events.detail: Two days ahead of the leaders' summit, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Homeland Security Adviser Stephen Miller, and SOUTHCOM commander Gen. Francis Donovan met regional defense ministers and military chiefs at SOUTHCOM headquarters in Doral to finalize the Joint Security Declaration underpinning the coalition.

events.title: Trump hosts founding summit, 17 nations sign Doral Charter
events.detail: President Trump convened Western Hemisphere leaders at Trump National Doral in Miami on 7 March 2026. Twelve heads of state attended in person (Argentina, Bolivia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guyana, Honduras, Panama, Paraguay, Trinidad and Tobago, and the US), with six more nations signing on (Bahamas, Belize, Chile, Guatemala, Jamaica, Peru), for 17 initial signatories to the Doral Charter. The summit launched both the diplomatic 'Shield of the Americas' forum and its operational military arm, the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition (A3C), with the motto 'We do bad things to bad people.' Kristi Noem was named special envoy.

events.title: Trump signs minerals deal alongside Chile's Kast at summit
events.detail: On the sidelines of the founding summit, Trump signed a critical-minerals cooperation agreement with newly inaugurated Chilean President José Antonio Kast, folding economic cooperation into the coalition's security-first agenda.

events.title: Díaz-Canel calls summit 'neocolonial'; Trump warns Cuba is 'at the end of the line'
events.detail: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel denounced the Doral summit as 'small,' 'reactionary,' and 'neocolonial,' accusing Washington of endorsing lethal force against sovereign governments' internal affairs. Trump responded at the summit by warning that Cuba's government was 'at the end of the line,' escalating rhetoric against Havana.

events.title: Region's three largest economies absent from founding summit
events.detail: Mexico, Brazil and Colombia — the hemisphere's three largest economies, all under left-leaning governments at the time — were not part of the founding signatories. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said she had rejected a US offer to send troops into Mexico against cartels, insisting Mexico would act on its own with only intelligence-sharing cooperation with Washington.

events.title: Bahamas, Belize, Guatemala, Jamaica and Chile formalize accession
events.detail: In the weeks following the founding summit, the Bahamas, Belize, Guatemala, Jamaica and Chile (under President José Antonio Kast) completed formal accession to the coalition, bringing total membership toward 18 as coordination mechanisms under SOUTHCOM's Joint Interagency Task Force-South began to stand up.

events.title: US forces strike suspected narco boat in eastern Pacific
events.detail: US forces conducted another lethal strike on a vessel suspected of drug trafficking in the eastern Pacific, part of the continuing Southern Spear campaign that member states cite as evidence of coalition resolve and critics cite as evidence of due-process violations.

events.title: Caribbean and eastern Pacific strikes kill 5
events.detail: US forces killed five people in separate strikes on suspected narco-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, continuing the near-weekly cadence of Southern Spear operations under the coalition's operational umbrella.

events.title: Lula refuses to designate cartels as terrorist organizations
events.detail: In a meeting with Trump, the US administration pressed Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to designate criminal organizations operating in Brazil as terrorist groups — a legal predicate the coalition has used elsewhere to justify lethal force. Lula refused, citing concerns about replicating patterns of US military dominance in the region and protecting Brazilian sovereignty.
events.confidenceReason: Reported by a single institutional source without a precise date; treated as approximate mid-2026 timing pending corroboration.

events.title: CNN investigation questions whether boat strikes are reducing cocaine flow
events.detail: A CNN analysis of the boat-strike campaign underpinning the coalition's operations found little evidence that the strikes had meaningfully reduced cocaine trafficking volumes, suggesting traffickers may simply be adapting routes and methods rather than being deterred.

events.title: Peru becomes 18th member under President Fujimori
events.detail: Peru, under President Keiko Fujimori, formally joined the coalition in early August 2026, becoming its 18th member ahead of the second A3C ministerial forum in Panama.

era: Colombia Crisis, Panama Forum & Ground-Ops Escalation (Aug 2026)

events.title: De la Espriella sworn in, vows to join coalition on day one
events.detail: Right-wing outsider Abelardo de la Espriella was inaugurated as Colombia's president on 7 August 2026 after narrowly defeating left-wing senator Iván Cepeda in the runoff, vowing a crackdown on armed groups and confirming that Colombia would join the Shield of the Americas on his first day in office — reversing predecessor Gustavo Petro's refusal to join.

events.title: De la Espriella proposes Medellín as Colombia's coalition operations hub
events.detail: As part of a broader decentralization push, De la Espriella proposed that Colombia's participation in the coalition — coordination, liaison, and possible basing functions — be run out of Medellín rather than Bogotá.

events.title: 7.4–7.5 magnitude earthquake strikes Chocó, over 300 dead
events.detail: A major earthquake struck Colombia's Chocó department on 10 August 2026, killing at least 312 people, injuring more than 4,600, and leaving hundreds missing, with damage extending to Cali, Pereira, Quibdó, Manizales and Armenia. The disaster struck days into De la Espriella's presidency and became the backdrop for an expanded US security and assistance offer.

events.title: Trump pledges $1B security package, 'Plan Colombia 2.0'
events.detail: Following the earthquake and De la Espriella's request for expanded joint operations, Trump announced a $1 billion security assistance package for Colombia, quickly dubbed 'Plan Colombia 2.0' by observers. Sanctions imposed on outgoing president Gustavo Petro, his wife, son, and interior minister by the US Treasury's OFAC in October 2025 over alleged drug-trade links remained in force even as Washington rebuilt military cooperation with the new government.
events.confidenceReason: US and Colombian officials confirm the pledge; exact disbursement terms not yet public.

events.title: Second A3C ministerial forum convenes in Panama
events.detail: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, as A3C chairman, led the coalition's second ministerial forum in Panama on 12 August 2026, addressing defense ministers and chiefs from 18 partner nations (Argentina, Bahamas, Belize, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Guyana, Honduras, Jamaica, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago) on operationalizing the coalition against narco-terrorism. He met bilaterally with Panamanian President José Mulino on Panama Canal security.

events.title: Colombia formally becomes 19th coalition member
events.detail: Hegseth announced during the Panama forum that Colombia had officially joined the Shield of the Americas as its 19th member, opening the possibility of joint Colombia-US strikes against narco-terrorist groups on Colombian soil. Colombia's request for joint military operations marked the coalition's deepest operational commitment to date from a new member.
events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by US Secretary of War statement (Tier 1-adjacent Tier 2 reporting); scope of joint-operations authorization not independently confirmed as of 20 Aug 2026.

events.title: Coalition sets November deadline for A3C campaign plan
events.detail: Hegseth told the Panama forum: 'Between now and November, we are going to write an A3C campaign plan... We will staff it with our teammates and our members here in the room, and we'll approve it by November.' SOUTHCOM commander Gen. Francis Donovan said members agreed on next steps including refining priority-network campaign plans, assigning lead nations, and standing up working groups. SCHEDULED — the campaign plan has not yet been drafted or approved as of 20 August 2026.

events.title: Hegseth joins PANAMAX 2026 canal-defense exercise
events.detail: On 13 August 2026 Hegseth participated in PANAMAX 2026, SOUTHCOM's premier multinational exercise focused on collective defense of the Panama Canal, held alongside the A3C ministerial and framed as evidence of the coalition's operational reach into critical infrastructure protection.

events.title: Hegseth reaffirms 'Trump Corollary,' calls for ground attacks on cartels
events.detail: Closing the Panama forum, Hegseth explicitly reaffirmed the 'Trump Corollary' to the Monroe Doctrine and called on regional partners to escalate beyond maritime interdiction to ground operations against cartel networks, drawing criticism from regional analysts about mission creep and sovereignty concerns among member states.

events.title: SOUTHCOM activates permanent Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere
events.detail: US Southern Command commander Gen. Francis Donovan activated Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere (JTF-WHEM), a standing operational headquarters under US Marine Corps Maj. Gen. Kevin Jarrard, replacing the ad hoc Joint Task Force Southern Spear as the command's principal formation for counter-narco-terrorist operations. JTF-WHEM is designed to integrate military capabilities with the 18 A3C partner nations at the time of stand-up, ahead of Colombia's accession as the 19th member.

events.title: Donovan calls to impose 'total systemic friction' on cartel networks; read as warning to Havana
events.detail: Addressing defense officials from A3C partner nations at the Panama forum, Gen. Francis Donovan said 'we need to attack these networks, we have to apply total systemic friction against them,' asking whether the coalition was 'willing to take the fight to the enemy.' Donovan did not name Cuba, but Cuban-diaspora and regional outlets read the remarks — combined with Trump-era rhetoric and the January 2026 Venezuela precedent — as an implicit warning to Havana over alleged links between Cuban officials and drug trafficking.

media.caption: SOUTHCOM commander Gen. Francis Donovan addresses the Panama A3C forum

events.confidenceReason: Donovan's remarks did not name Cuba explicitly; SOUTHCOM has not confirmed Cuba as a specific target, so the 'warning to Havana' framing is a media interpretation rather than an official statement.

events.title: Hegseth: Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras agree to joint ground operations — Guatemala denies
events.detail: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras had agreed to allow US forces to conduct joint ground operations against cartel and 'terrorist' networks on their soil, extending the maritime Southern Spear strike campaign — which the AP tallies at more than 200 killed in over 60 boat strikes — onto land, following a similar arrangement with Ecuador launched in March 2026. Guatemalan President Bernardo Arévalo publicly denied any such agreement, saying Guatemala's constitution bars joint military operations with foreign forces and that Guatemala had only requested training, tactical planning support and intelligence sharing. Honduras and Colombia did not respond to AP's requests for comment on Hegseth's claim.

media.caption: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth speaks at the A3C forum in Panama City, 12 Aug 2026

events.confidenceReason: Guatemala's president explicitly denied the agreement on the record; Honduras and Colombia have neither confirmed nor denied Hegseth's characterization as of 21 Aug 2026.
